speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; to narrow down the cause, are these symptoms sudden in onset or did they develop gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your progressive weakness, significant weight loss, and history of smoking, I am concerned about potential malignancy or severe neuropathy. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC), Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP), and Tumor Marker Panel (CEA, CA 19-9). Do you have any numbness or tingling in your hand or foot as well?

speaker: Doctor
text: The CBC results are normal, and you have denied distal numbness in your hands or feet. Given your significant weight loss, diabetes, and anabolic steroid use, does the weakness in your right arm follow a specific nerve distribution, such as the ulnar or radial nerve?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: The burning and dull aching pain combined with weakness and decreased sensation suggests a radiculopathy or a focal neuropathy rather than a distal polyneuropathy. Given your history of steroid use, does the weakness involve the shoulder girdle muscles (deltoid, biceps) or is it more proximal?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Diabetes Social history: Drinks 2-7 alcoholic beverages per day. Has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes per day since he was 25. Uses anabolic steroids.

speaker: Doctor
text: The burning pain and significant weight loss suggest a severe compressive radiculopathy, possibly exacerbated by your diabetes and steroid use. REQUEST TEST: Cervical Spine MRI. Is the weakness and pain primarily in the deltoid and biceps muscles?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor) causing right arm weakness, decreased sensation, and burning pain via compressive radiculopathy.
